name: Rituximab exposure and CD19+ B-cell response
description: Starting configurations for exploring rituximab persistence, CD19+ B-cell depletion, and immune-cell repopulation with typical or individualized PK/PD parameters.

scenarios.name: Exact Monolix archive parameter/result anchor
scenarios.description: No-dose replay of final model 3 population estimates, likelihood criteria, and subject-1 exported prediction endpoints.

scenarios.name: Typical 1000 mg exposure and B-cell response
scenarios.description: Explore rituximab persistence, CD19+ B-cell depletion, and gradual repopulation over 200 days using the typical parameter set.
scientific_questions: How long does circulating rituximab persist after the starting 1000 mg administration?
How rapidly and deeply are CD19+ B cells depleted?
Which clearance, drug–cell coupling, and turnover parameters shift B-cell recovery timing?
interpretation_guardrails: Interpret this as a deterministic typical-parameter trajectory, not a population distribution.
The starting administration is encoded as C(0) = dose/V; repeat-dose events are not represented in this released setup.
Do not use the simulated CD19+ trajectory as a clinical dosing recommendation.

scenarios.name: Individualized exposure and B-cell response
scenarios.description: Explore how an individualized PK/PD parameter set changes rituximab exposure, CD19+ B-cell depletion, and recovery relative to the typical configuration.
scientific_questions: How does this individualized parameter set change rituximab persistence relative to the typical configuration?
How do the individualized depletion and turnover terms shift the depth and duration of B-cell depletion?
Which differences are driven by exposure and which are driven by B-cell dynamics?
interpretation_guardrails: This configuration demonstrates individual-parameter behavior; it is not a prospective patient-specific dosing workflow.
The starting administration is encoded as C(0) = dose/V; repeat-dose events are not represented in this released setup.
Do not infer clinical benefit or an optimal redosing time from CD19+ cell count alone.
